definition.def: If someone or something satisfies you, they give you enough of what you want or need to make you pleased or contented.
examples: The pace of change has not been quick enough to satisfy everyone. [VERB noun]
We just can't find enough good second-hand cars to satisfy demand. [VERB noun]
The scandal stories satisfy people's curiosity for a few hours. [VERB noun]

definition.def: To satisfy someone that something is true or has been done properly means to convince them by giving them more information or by showing them what has been done.
examples: He has to satisfy the environmental lobby that real progress will be made to cut emissions. [VERB noun that]
He wanted to satisfy himself that he had given his best performance. [VERB noun that]

definition.def: If you satisfy the requirements for something, you are good enough or have the right qualities to fulfil these requirements.
examples: The procedures should satisfy certain basic requirements. [VERB noun]

examples.sentence: Because of the need to boost production and satisfy Europe's ever-increasing appetite for cinnamon, the Dutch began to alter the harvesting practices of the Ceylonese.

Since sharks cannot detect from electro-reception whether or not something will satisfy their tastes, they tend to "try before they buy", taking one or two bites and then assessing the results (our sinewy muscle does not compare well with plumper, softer prey such as seals).
Coffee was grown in ever increasing quantities to satisfy the growing demand from Europe, and it became nearly as important as sugar production, which was grown under very similar conditions.
Following our fire safety inspection, the front doors of individual flats were upgraded or replaced in order to satisfy fire safety regulations.
We welcome your interest in joining our sixth form and look forward to offering you a place if you satisfy our minimum entry requirements.
